title_en: Xinjiang Yakun Trading Co., Ltd. v. Xinjiang Jinghe County Kangrui Cotton Processing Co., Ltd. — dispute over a sales contract
ruling_gist_en: In adjudicating contract dispute cases, when determining the liability for damages of the breaching party, the 'foreseeability principle' shall be followed, i.e., the breaching party shall only be liable for the losses caused to the other party by its breach, and shall not be liable for losses that are unforeseeable by both parties due to market risks or other factors, caused by the non-breaching party's fault, and without causal relationship with the breach.
keywords_en: Civil;Sales contract dispute;Second instance;Supreme People's Court;Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region;Legal person;Contract Law;Scope of liability for breach of contract;Foreseeability principle;Determination of market risk losses;Partial support;Cotton purchase and sale;Non-conforming quality;Weight shortage;Resale loss;Contract dispute;Sales contract;Sales contract dispute of a processing limited company
full_text_en:
Xinjiang Yakun Commercial Co., Ltd. v. Xinjiang Jinghe County Kangrui Cotton Processing Co., Ltd. — Dispute over a Sales Contract

Ruling Summary

In adjudicating contract dispute cases, the determination of the defaulting party's liability for damages shall follow the "foreseeability principle," i.e., the defaulting party shall only bear liability for damages for losses caused to the other party by its breach of contract. For losses caused by factors such as market risks that neither party could foresee, which are not attributable to the non-defaulting party's fault and have no causal relationship with the breach, the defaulting party shall not bear liability for damages.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2006) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 111

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Xinjiang Yakun Commercial Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Room 7, 1st Floor, Building 1, Taicui City Garden, Beijing Road, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Qiao Fengjin, Executive Director of the company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ke, Supervisor of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zou Jianzhang, Deputy Manager of the company.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Xinjiang Jinghe County Kangrui Cotton Processing Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Er Muchang, Daheyanzi Town, Jinghe County, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Li Songcai, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhou Ling, Attorney at Beijing Baolong Law Firm.

Both appellants, Yakun Commercial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yakun Company) and Xinjiang Jinghe County Kangrui Cotton Processing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kangrui Company), appealed against the Civil Judgment (2004) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 114 of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region to this Court. In accordance with the law, this Court formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Wu Qingbao, Judge Jia Wei, and Acting Judge Sha Ling to hear the case. Court Clerk Yuan Hongxia served as recorder. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region found the following facts upon trial: On January 2, 2004, Yakun Company and Kangrui Company entered into a Cotton Purchase and Sales Contract, stipulating that Kangrui Company would supply Yakun Company with 1,370 tons of Grade 229 (Grade 2) ginned cotton at a unit price of RMB 16,900 per ton. The quality of the ginned cotton was to be in accordance with the national cotton quality standard GB1103-1999. Kangrui Company was to be fully responsible for quality and weight; in the event of major quality or weight issues, the matter was to be determined by notarized inspection. Payment method: Yakun Company was to first prepay RMB 10 million as a deposit, and the balance was to be transferred to Kangrui Company's account by January 15, 2004. Default liability: If one party failed to perform its obligations under the contract, the other party had the right to unilaterally terminate the contract, and the defaulting party was to pay liquidated damages to the other party in the amount of 10% of the value of the unperformed portion of the contract. After the contract was signed, Yakun Company paid RMB 6.5 million as advance payment to Kangrui Company on the same day. Kangrui Company commenced delivery upon receipt of the advance payment. During Yakun Company's process of taking delivery, Kangrui Company notified Yakun Company that the warehouse only had 1,147.535 tons of ginned cotton, and requested Yakun Company to temporarily pay based on that quantity. On January 7, 2004, Kangrui Company, in accordance with the contract, shipped to Yakun Company 52 batches (260 bales per batch), totaling 13,518 bales of ginned cotton, weighing a total of 1,173.947 tons (including 3,900 bales of Grade 1 cotton, weighing 337.109 tons; and 9,620 bales of Grade 2 cotton, weighing 836.838 tons), to a storage location designated by Yakun Company, and submitted to Yakun Company the factory inspection reports for all batches of ginned cotton. Yakun Company transferred the remaining payment of RMB 12,893,348.4 into Kangrui Company's account by January 12, 2004.

On June 12, 2004, Yakun Company entered into a contract for the purchase and sale of 800 tons of pure cotton yarn with Guangdong Jinxing Cloth Co., Ltd., and subsequently entered into two entrusted processing contracts with Xinjiang Bozhou Textile (Group) Co., Ltd. for 200 tons of 32-count yarn and 200 tons of 40-count yarn, respectively. To perform these two entrusted processing contracts, in mid-June 2004, Yakun Company transferred 10 batches of 2,600 bales (89.955 tons of Grade 1 ginned cotton; 135.224 tons of Grade 2 ginned cotton), totaling 225.179 tons of ginned cotton delivered by Kangrui Company, to Xinjiang Bozhou Cotton Textile Co., Ltd. for spinning. On July 2, 2004, following notarized inspection by the Bozhou Fiber Inspection Institute, it was found that the quality grades of these 10 batches of ginned cotton did not match the quality grades indicated on Kangrui Company's factory inspection certificates. The notarized inspection conclusions were: Grade 2 ginned cotton: 1.618 tons; Grade 3 ginned cotton: 172.008 tons; Grade 4 ginned cotton: 35.676 tons; total weight: 209.302 tons. The weight difference compared to the original factory ginned cotton inspection certificates was -15.877 tons.

Yakun Company sold 8 batches totaling 2,080 bales (including 1,560 bales of Grade 1 ginned cotton, totaling 135.022 tons; 520 bales of Grade 2 ginned cotton, totaling 45.704 tons), with a total weight of 180.726 tons of ginned cotton delivered by Kangrui Company, to Sichuan Cotton and Hemp Group Co., Ltd. On July 19, 2004, following inspection by the Sichuan Province Fiber Inspection Bureau, the conclusions were: Grade 3 ginned cotton: 166.439 tons; Grade 4 ginned cotton: 4.944 tons; total weight: 171.383 tons. The weight difference compared to the original factory ginned cotton inspection certificates was -9.343 tons. On October 25, 2004, Sichuan Cotton and Hemp Company settled payment to Yakun Company for the 171.383 tons of ginned cotton sold to it at a unit price of RMB 13,660.99 per ton, totaling RMB 2,391,479.3.

On May 21, 2004, Yakun Company entered into a cotton purchase and sale contract with Hubei Macheng Shenlong Textile Industry Co., Ltd. Yakun Company sold and shipped 2 batches totaling 520 bales of ginned cotton (Grade 2 ginned cotton), with a total weight of 45.556 tons, delivered by Kangrui Company, to Hubei Macheng Shenlong Textile Industry Co., Ltd. On June 10, 2004, following notarized inspection of these two batches of ginned cotton by the Huanggang City Fiber Inspection Institute, Hubei Province, the notarized inspection conclusions were: Grade 3 ginned cotton: 33.782 tons; Grade 4 ginned cotton: 8.924 tons; total weight: 42.706 tons. The weight difference compared to the original factory ginned cotton inspection certificates was -2.85 tons. Due to grade discrepancies, Macheng Shenlong Textile Industry Co., Ltd. requested a return.

Accordingly, Yakun Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting a judgment: to rescind the cotton purchase and sale contract signed by both parties; Kangrui Company to refund Yakun Company the payment of RMB 19,393,348.4; to return the deposit of RMB 4.6 million; and to bear the litigation costs.

During the first-instance trial, with the approval of the court of first instance: (1) In early November 2004, Yakun Company sold 32 batches totaling 8,318 bales (including 1,300 bales of Grade 1 ginned cotton, totaling 112.132 tons; 7,020 bales of Grade 2 ginned cotton, totaling 610.354 tons), with a total weight of 722.486 tons of ginned cotton delivered by Kangrui Company, to Xinjiang Jinfang Textile Co., Ltd. On November 24, 2004, following notarized inspection by the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Fiber Inspection Bureau, the conclusions were: Grade 3 ginned cotton: 151.187 tons; Grade 4 ginned cotton: 514.981 tons; Grade 5 ginned cotton: 21.643 tons; total weight: 687.811 tons. The weight difference compared to the original factory ginned cotton inspection certificates was -34.675 tons. On December 7, 2004, Yakun Company entered into a cotton purchase and sale contract with Xinjiang Jinfang Textile Co., Ltd., with the transaction prices set at RMB 11,000 per ton for Grade 3 cotton, RMB 10,400 per ton for Grade 4 cotton, and RMB 10,200 per ton for Grade 5 cotton. Xinjiang Jinfang Textile Co., Ltd. settled payment to Yakun Company totaling RMB 2,237,922.28. (2) On February 2, 2005, Yakun Company entered into a cotton purchase and sale contract with Urumqi Sanhetai Commercial Co., Ltd., selling the 209.302 tons of ginned cotton that had been shipped to Xinjiang Bozhou Cotton Textile Co., Ltd. for spinning to Urumqi Sanhetai Commercial Co., Ltd. at a unit price of RMB 11,000, for a total sales amount of RMB 2,302,322.

Based on the above, according to the notarized inspection certificates and cotton inspection certificates for ginned cotton, the total quantity of ginned cotton supplied by Kangrui Company to Yakun Company was: Grade 2 ginned cotton: 1.618 tons; Grade 3 ginned cotton: 523.416 tons; Grade 4 ginned cotton: 564.525 tons; Grade 5 ginned cotton: 21.643 tons; total weight: 1,111.202 tons. The total sales revenue was RMB 12,733,990.29, and the loss of Yakun Company's principal payment was RMB 6,659,358.11.

The court of first instance held, upon trial, that the cotton purchase and sale contract signed by Yakun Company and Kangrui Company on January 2, 2004, represented the true intentions of both parties, complied with relevant legal provisions, was lawful and valid, and should be protected by law. Both parties were required to strictly perform their respective obligations in accordance with the contract. Yakun Company performed its obligation to pay the price in accordance with the contract. Kangrui Company should have performed its obligation to deliver the goods to Yakun Company in accordance with the quality and quantity standards specified in the contract. Pursuant to Article 4 of the cotton purchase and sale contract signed by both parties: the supplier is to be fully responsible for quality and weight; in the event of major quality or weight issues, the matter is to be determined by notarized inspection. Therefore, Kangrui Company remained fully responsible for quality and weight issues concerning the cotton supplied to Yakun Company, even at the time of its transfer. In the actual performance of the contract in this case, the ginned cotton delivered by Kangrui Company to Yakun Company had serious quality and quantity issues, resulting in the inability to perform the entrusted processing contracts for 32-count yarn and 40-count yarn between Yakun Company and Xinjiang Bozhou Textile (Group) Co., Ltd. The purpose of the contract for Yakun Company could not be realized. Kangrui Company's conduct constituted a fundamental breach of contract. Accordingly, Yakun Company's request to rescind the contract was in accordance with the law and the agreement of the parties, and the court supported it. After Yakun Company took delivery of this cotton, the market price of cotton underwent significant changes, with prices beginning to decline month by month. To prevent losses from the price decline on this batch of cotton, by February 7, 2005, Yakun Company had sold all the cotton delivered by Kangrui Company, making mutual restitution impossible. Although remedial measures were taken in response to the market price fluctuation of cotton, Yakun Company nevertheless suffered a certain loss of funds. Kangrui Company should bear primary liability for damages for the loss of principal suffered by Yakun Company. Under the circumstances of a significant decline in cotton prices, Yakun Company failed to take timely measures and was dilatory in selling, thereby missing the optimal time for cotton sales. Yakun Company also bore some fault for the loss of principal on this batch of cotton and should correspondingly bear its own liability. Regarding the deposit issue: The deposit is a contract of a practical nature; the deposit contract takes effect upon actual delivery of the deposit. The RMB 6.5 million paid by Yakun Company to Kangrui Company on January 2, 2004, was indicated on the remittance slip as an advance purchase payment, not as a deposit. Pursuant to Article 118 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, "Where a party delivers a retention deposit, security deposit, guarantee deposit, earnest money, earnest money bond, or deposit, etc., but does not stipulate the nature of a deposit, and the party claims the right to a deposit, the People's Court shall not support it." Therefore, Yakun Company's claim for Kangrui Company to pay RMB 4.6 million in accordance with the deposit penalty rule lacked factual and legal basis, and the court did not support it. In conclusion, the court, pursuant to Article 94(4) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Contract Law") and Article 90 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment: 1. The cotton purchase and sale contract signed by Yakun Company and Kangrui Company on January 2, 2004, is rescinded; 2. Kangrui Company shall compensate Yakun Company for 70% of the loss of principal on the cotton, i.e., RMB 4,661,550.67, to be paid in a lump sum within 15 days after this judgment takes effect. Yakun Company shall bear the remaining loss. 3. Yakun Company's claim for Kangrui Company to return the deposit of RMB 4.6 million is dismissed. The first-instance court acceptance fee of RMB 129,976.74 and preservation fee of RMB 50,520, totaling RMB 180,496.74, shall be borne by Kangrui Company in the amount of RMB 126,347.72 and by Yakun Company in the amount of RMB 54,149.02.

Both Yakun Company and Kangrui Company, dissatisfied with the aforesaid civil judgment of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, appealed to this Court. Yakun Company appealed, arguing: 1. Regarding the deposit issue. In this case, both parties not only signed a clear written deposit contract but also actually performed it. The court of first instance improperly denied that the payment was a deposit merely because Yakun Company indicated on the remittance slip that the sum was an advance purchase payment. The deposit was agreed upon by both parties; the nature of the deposit contract cannot be changed solely based on the purpose indicated on a single remittance slip. Therefore, Kangrui Company should bear full liability for fundamental breach and deposit liability, i.e., to compensate for the loss of principal up to RMB 19,393,348.4, plus transportation costs and interest totaling RMB 1,087,678.99, pending settlement of interest on the weight shortfall (i.e., the appellant's purchase payment plus transportation costs and pending settlement interest), and at the same time return the deposit of RMB 4.6 million double. 2. Regarding compensation for losses. Since the judgment of first instance found the fact and nature of fundamental breach, Kangrui Company should bear the liability for fundamental breach and apply the deposit penalty rule, i.e., compensate for all losses and then apply the deposit penalty rule. Even following the logic of the first-instance judgment, which denies the deposit penalty rule and instead shifts to compensating Yakun Company's losses, the losses caused to Yakun Company by Kangrui Company's breach are by no means limited to the loss of principal found by the court. Yakun Company's direct losses at least include: price difference loss on the goods of RMB 6,152,857.22; loss on cotton weight shortfall of RMB 1,060,233.67 and pending settlement interest loss; bank loan interest of RMB 8,380.8; loan interest of RMB 712,745.97; goods freight of RMB 291,126.22; litigation costs of RMB 129,976.74; and litigation preservation fee of RMB 50,520. 3. Yakun Company's purpose in purchasing the cotton was not for resale but for processing. Faced with a market situation of a sharp decline in cotton prices not seen for many years, Yakun Company sold the cotton in a timely manner to prevent further expansion of losses. Yakun Company was not at fault subjectively and took proactive responsive measures objectively. Therefore, the finding of the court of first instance that Yakun Company was dilatory in selling was without factual basis, and the allocation of liability between the parties at a ratio of 70% to 30% was also without legal basis. Yakun Company requested the court of second instance to amend the judgment by ruling that Kangrui Company compensate Yakun Company for the loss of principal up to RMB 19,393,348.4, plus transportation costs and interest totaling RMB 1,087,678.99 and pending settlement interest (i.e., the appellant's purchase payment plus transportation costs and pending settlement interest), and at the same time return the deposit of RMB 4.6 million double, or alternatively, compensate for all losses resulting from the fundamental breach, totaling RMB 8,481,266.62 plus pending settlement interest, and have Kangrui Company bear the appellate costs of this case.

Kangrui Company appealed, arguing: 1. The evidence on which the first-instance judgment relied, specifically the "Notarized Inspection Certificates," was insufficient to find that Kangrui Company's supply was of non-conforming quality, and those inspection certificates were not binding on Kangrui Company. The Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Cotton Quality promulgated by the State Council and the Procedures and Inspection Regulations for Commercial Cotton National Notarized Inspection of the China Fiber Inspection Bureau stipulate that either party to a cotton transaction should request notarized inspection before settlement of the cotton transaction. However, the inspection certificates relied on by the judgment were all conducted six or twelve months after the transaction between Kangrui Company and Yakun Company. These inspections only evidenced the quality of the cotton at the time of Yakun Company's subsequent transaction, not the quality of the cotton at the time of the transaction between Kangrui Company and Yakun Company. As cotton has a shelf life, even in a flawless storage environment, degradation in quality and weight is inevitable; if the storage environment is poor, it may accelerate degradation. Therefore, relevant national regulations specifically require that inspections be requested before transaction settlement. If the cotton involved in this case was indeed supplied by Kangrui Company, it is a normal natural phenomenon for grade declines and weight losses to occur after such a long period. 2. The finding of the first-instance judgment regarding the purpose of the contract in this case was erroneous, and the application of legal provisions for contract rescission was incorrect. The purpose of the Cotton Purchase and Sale Contract between Yakun Company and Kangrui Company was for Yakun Company to purchase cotton from Kangrui Company as agreed in the contract. The price at which it would be sold to a third party is the purpose of a different contract. After the contract in this case was signed, Yakun Company raised no issues regarding quantity or quality. Payment and goods were settled, and the transaction was effectively completed. The purpose of the contract between Kangrui Company and Yakun Company was realized, and there were no legal conditions for rescission. In summary, the first-instance judgment erred in fact-finding and application of law. It improperly shifted the business risk of Yakun Company onto Kangrui Company, which was without legal basis. Kangrui Company requested that the judgment be reversed, Yakun Company's claims be dismissed, and Yakun Company bear all litigation costs of the first and second instances.

In response to Kangrui Company's grounds of appeal, Yakun Company argued in its defense: Pursuant to Article 14 of the Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Cotton Quality: When a cotton business operator sells cotton to a cotton-consuming enterprise, any party to the transaction may, before settlement of the cotton transaction, entrust a professional fiber inspection institution to conduct notarized inspection of the cotton being traded; after notarized inspection, the professional fiber inspection institution shall issue a cotton quality notarized inspection certificate, which serves as the basis for cotton quality and quantity. This regulation clearly uses "may" rather than "shall." Regarding the impact of the time interval on cotton quality, Yakun Company argued that cotton products have no specified shelf life. The inspection reports conducted six months after the transaction showed consistent quality conclusions, and there was no difference in cotton quality due to the time interval. Regarding the realization of the contract purpose, the judgment of the first instance found that Yakun Company's contract purpose was not realized and that Kangrui Company's conduct constituted a fundamental breach. The contract purpose referred to here is the purpose of Yakun Company in entering into the contract, not the mere settlement of payment and goods. Whether payment and goods were settled has absolutely nothing to do with whether the contract purpose was realized. Regarding whether the sales opportunity was missed, Yakun Company discovered serious quality and weight issues in Kangrui Company's goods during processing and sales. At that time, the price was not unfavorable; it was not, as Kangrui Company claimed, that Yakun Company failed to sell when market prices were high. The legal conditions for contract rescission stipulated in Article 94 of the Contract Law never required that the cotton could not be sold. Furthermore, Article 97 of the Contract Law further provides: After rescission of a contract, if the contract has not been performed, performance shall be terminated; if it has been performed, the parties may, based on the circumstances of performance and the nature of the contract, request restoration to the original state, take other remedial measures, and have the right to claim compensation for losses. According to the explicit provisions of this article, a party may choose among "requesting restoration to the original state, taking other remedial measures, and having the right to claim compensation for losses." In conclusion, Yakun Company requested the court of second instance to support its appeal claims.

Kangrui Company, in response to Yakun Company's grounds for appeal, argued as follows: First, Yakun Company's claim for application of the deposit forfeiture rule is inconsistent with the facts, conflicts with the agreement between the parties, and lacks legal basis. Yakun Company did not actually perform its obligation to pay the deposit. The "Cotton Purchase and Sale Contract" between Kangrui Company and Yakun Company stipulated that Yakun Company should "prepay a deposit of RMB 10 million," but on the day the contract was signed, Yakun Company only paid RMB 6.5 million for the goods (the bank remittance slip clearly indicated "prepaid payment for goods"). This payment differed from the contract in both nature and amount. Yakun Company's strained argument that this payment constituted a deposit has no factual basis and cannot be accepted. Kangrui Company has fully performed its contractual obligations, and Yakun Company's request for application of the deposit forfeiture rule lacks legal basis. Issues of quantity and quality should fall under the scope of liability for breach of contract and are not subject to the deposit forfeiture rule. Second, the notarized inspection certificates submitted by Yakun Company to the court were all obtained from notarized inspections submitted unilaterally by Yakun Company six months or one year after the contract was fully performed. These certificates are procedurally improper and substantively incapable of proving the quantity and quality of the cotton at the time of the transaction between Kangrui Company and Yakun Company. The inspection results are not binding on Kangrui Company. After the transaction between Kangrui Company and Yakun Company was completed, Yakun Company did not contact Kangrui Company for as long as half a year, let alone raise any quality issues. In June, after a sharp market downturn, Yakun Company contacted Kangrui Company only to discuss sharing losses. In this case, Kangrui Company was never notified of the notarized inspections that produced the certificates submitted by Yakun Company. The earliest notarized inspection certificate submitted by Yakun Company was dated July 2004, which was the final time for grade reduction of cotton from a production year. Inspecting the cotton at that time would inevitably and normally result in a reduction of one to two grades compared to the time of the transaction, but this does not indicate the quality grade of the cotton at the time of the transaction between Kangrui Company and Yakun Company. Yakun Company's request to rescind the contract on grounds of quality issues half a year after settlement with Kangrui Company is inconsistent with relevant regulations and practices for cotton trading and lacks legal basis. Third, the contractual provision "responsible for quality and weight to the end" should be limited to the time of full performance of the contract. Fourth, Yakun Company has sold all of the batch of cotton. The judgment's finding that the purpose of the contract was defeated is erroneous, and the application of legal provisions on rescission of contract is incorrect. In summary, the judgment of first instance erred in fact-finding and application of law, improperly shifting Yakun Company's operational risks to Kangrui Company without legal basis. We request that the court of second instance reject Yakun Company's claims in accordance with law.

Upon investigation in the second instance, in addition to confirming the facts found by the court of first instance, this court also found the following: On November 15, 2005, the court of first instance conducted an investigation with Xinjiang Cotton and Jute Company regarding issues such as cotton trading prices in 2004. The General Manager of that company, Xu Yanyi, stated that in January 2004, first-grade cotton was RMB 17,500/ton, fell to RMB 12,500/ton by May-June, dropped to RMB 11,000/ton by August, and rebounded to approximately RMB 13,000/ton by April 2005. The price difference between each grade of cotton was approximately RMB 200. The "year" for cotton runs from September each year to August 31 of the following year. During this year, the cotton should be guaranteed not to deteriorate, but by around October of the following year, even notarially inspected cotton would be downgraded by one to two grades.

On July 31, 2006, this court telephoned Yakun Company and Kangrui Company to inquire about the price difference between each grade of cotton. The agents ad litem of both Yakun Company and Kangrui Company stated that when the cotton market was good, the price difference per grade was about RMB 200.

Furthermore, an excerpt from the internet, derived from an article titled "Review of the 2004 Cotton Market and Outlook for the 2005 Market" published in the *Futures Daily* on December 28, 2004, indicated: Due to the reduction in cotton production in 2003, domestic cotton sales prices once surged to the level of RMB 17,500/ton. This price spike was influenced by both the factor of an expanding gap between production and demand and the panic psychology of "buying on a rising market, not on a falling one." Under the guidance of macroeconomic control policies such as the two tranches of a total additional issuance of 1.5 million tons of quotas and the tightening of credit, domestic cotton prices fell. Cotton sales prices dropped to RMB 15,000/ton in June of that year. Subsequently, influenced by market expectations of a bumper cotton harvest in 2004, the decline in domestic cotton prices accelerated and broke through several psychological barriers. At present, domestic cotton sales prices have fallen to RMB 11,300/ton, a decrease of 35% from the beginning of the year.

This court holds that the "Cotton Purchase and Sale Contract" signed by the parties to this case on January 2, 2004, represents the true intention of each party and does not violate national laws or administrative regulations, and therefore should be deemed valid. This case is a dispute over a cotton sales contract. Based on the grounds of appeal of both parties, the main focus of the dispute in this case is whether the quality and quantity of the cotton in question conformed to the contract, whether Yakun Company suffered losses, and how such losses should be calculated. At the same time, the parties also dispute the determination of the deposit and whether the contract should be rescinded.

1. Regarding the determination of the quantity and quality of delivered goods. According to the factory *Inspection Certificate* for the cotton submitted by Kangrui Company to Yakun Company on January 7, 2004, Kangrui Company should have delivered 1,173.947 tons of cotton to Yakun Company, including 337.109 tons of first-grade cotton and 836.838 tons of second-grade cotton. After receiving this batch of goods, Yakun Company raised no objections and settled accounts with Kangrui Company on January 12 of the same year. After June 2004, Yakun Company gradually sold this batch of cotton to customers in Guangdong, Sichuan, Hubei and other places, and the local fiber inspection institutes issued new notarized inspection certificates for this batch of cotton. By the end of 2004, the notarized inspection certificates showed that the total amount of cotton actually delivered by Kangrui Company to Yakun Company in this batch was 1,111.202 tons, including 1.618 tons of second-grade cotton, 523.416 tons of third-grade cotton, 564.525 tons of fourth-grade cotton, and 21.643 tons of fifth-grade cotton. Since notarized inspection certificates are the basis for determining cotton quality and quantity, and Kangrui Company promised in the contract to be responsible for quality and weight to the end, with issues regarding quality and weight to be determined by notarized inspection. Furthermore, according to Article 8.4 of the *National Standard GB1103-1999 Cotton - Fine Lint Cotton*, which states that "The validity period of a cotton inspection certificate is one year, calculated from the date of issuance. Cotton that exceeds the validity period of the certificate shall be re-inspected, and a certificate shall be issued based on the re-inspection results," Kangrui Company must uphold its promise regarding the quality and weight of the sold cotton within one year, according to the standards stated in the *Inspection Certificate* it issued to Yakun Company on January 7, 2004. Based on this, comparing the *Cotton Purchase and Sale Contract* and the *Inspection Certificate* with the *Notarized Inspection Certificates*, Kangrui Company delivered 62.745 tons less lint cotton to Yakun Company; the cotton grade was downgraded from the second grade promised in the *Cotton Purchase and Sale Contract* and *Inspection Certificate* to third and fourth grades. This quality downgrade and weight shortage not only constitutes a breach of contract but also caused actual losses to Yakun Company. For this, Kangrui Company shall compensate Yakun Company based on the contract price and the market conditions at the time of the transaction between the parties.

2. Regarding compensation for losses due to cotton weight shortage. Kangrui Company and Yakun Company agreed in the contract that "quality requirements shall be implemented according to the national quality standard GB1103-1999" and "major issues regarding quality and weight shall be determined by notarized inspection." As mentioned above, Kangrui Company delivered 62.745 tons less lint cotton to Yakun Company. At the contract price of RMB 16,900/ton, Kangrui Company shall refund the principal of RMB 1,060,390 to Yakun Company, and compensate for interest losses calculated at the People's Bank of China contemporaneous demand deposit rate from January 12, 2004, until the date of actual payment. The judgment of first instance erred in not recognizing the loss due to weight shortage. This court corrects this. Appellant Yakun Company's ground of appeal that Kangrui Company should compensate it for the principal and interest of the cotton weight shortage loss is established, and this court supports it.

3. Regarding compensation for losses due to quality downgrade. The *Cotton Purchase and Sale Contract* in this case stipulated that Kangrui Company was to provide Yakun Company with 229-grade (second-grade) lint cotton at a unit price of RMB 16,900/ton. Based on the objective fact confirmed by the *Notarized Inspection Certificates* that the cotton generally dropped by one to two grades, and that Kangrui Company actually delivered 1,111.202 tons of cotton, and referring to the consultation with Xinjiang Cotton and Jute Company by the court of first instance and the inquiry made by the second-instance case handler with the agents ad litem of both parties, it should be determined that the price difference between cotton grades at the time of signing this contract was about RMB 200. Balancing the interests of both parties, this court determines the loss due to cotton grade downgrade to be RMB 400 x 1,111.202 tons = RMB 444,480.80, which shall be compensated by Kangrui Company to Yakun Company.

The judgment of first instance correctly found that Yakun Company suffered capital losses, but the standard for determining the scope of compensation was inappropriate. In January 2004, when this contract was signed, domestic cotton market prices soared, but after May-June 2004, cotton market prices fell, with a difference of RMB 5,000-6,000 per ton during this period. Even if the quality grade of the cotton remained unchanged, Yakun Company, which resold the cotton after June 2004, would inevitably suffer income losses due to market conditions. The principal loss of RMB 6,659,358.11 found by the court of first instance includes not only the price difference loss due to cotton grade downgrade but also the income loss caused by the market downturn during this period. This portion of income loss is clearly a risk of market conditions, unforeseeable by either party, and not caused by any fault of Kangrui Company. Since there is no causal relationship between Kangrui Company and this portion of the loss, Kangrui Company should not bear the income loss of Yakun Company caused by changes in market conditions. The judgment of first instance improperly treated the difference between the sales price formed by Yakun Company's resale during the market downturn and the purchase price formed during the market upturn as a loss to be shared by both parties. This is not only based on different contractual relationships but also violates the principles of fairness and fault liability. This court corrects this. Appellant Yakun Company's ground of appeal that Kangrui Company should compensate it for cotton income loss of RMB 6,152,857.22 cannot be established. This court confirms the actual losses suffered by Yakun Company when purchasing the cotton, i.e., the loss from cotton weight shortage and the price difference loss from quality downgrade. Other losses, i.e., the income loss due to market risk, transportation costs incurred during resale, and interest losses on loans with third parties, are not supported due to lack of contractual and legal basis.

4. Regarding whether the contract in this case should be rescinded. In this sales contract, the combined value of the cotton not delivered by Kangrui Company and the cotton not conforming to the contractual quality is RMB 1,504,870.80, accounting for approximately 8% of the total contract amount of RMB 19,393,348.40. Not only is the value of the breached portion low, but it also did not substantially deprive Yakun Company of the opportunity to profit from resale and did not affect the realization of the purpose of Yakun Company's contract. Yakun Company's assertion that its purpose in purchasing the cotton was not for resale but for processing is clearly inconsistent with the facts. Yakun Company actually purchased a total of 1,111.202 tons of cotton and only transferred 225.179 tons to Xinjiang Bozhou Cotton Textile Co., Ltd. for spinning and processing as long as five months after receiving the goods. Prior to this, Yakun Company had already resold a large amount of the cotton. Given that Yakun Company failed to submit corresponding evidence that all of the purchased cotton would be used for processing, its ground of appeal that the purpose of the contract could not be realized cannot be established. The loss due to breach of contract for quality downgrade can be remedied by cash compensation from Kangrui Company based on the cotton grade price difference at the time the contract was signed. Based on the fact that the sales contract between Kangrui Company and Yakun Company has been fully performed and Yakun Company has already sold all the cotton, this court holds that Kangrui Company's improper performance of the contract constitutes only an ordinary breach of contract, not a fundamental breach, and does not affect the realization of Yakun Company's purpose in the contract. It does not meet the statutory conditions for rescission of contract under Article 94 of the Contract Law. Therefore, the judgment of first instance ordering the rescission of the contract in this case is unnecessary, and this court corrects it.

5. Regarding the determination of the deposit. The judgment of first instance, based on the fact that the payment of RMB 6.5 million by Yakun Company was only recorded as payment for goods and not as a deposit, and applying Article 118 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the PRC*, found that Yakun Company did not pay a deposit to Kangrui Company. This finding of fact is clear and the application of law is correct. This court sustains it.

Considering the objective circumstances that Yakun Company raised quality issues only six months after settlement with Kangrui Company, that Kangrui Company was not notified to be present for the notarized inspections, that cotton quality can change and degrade over time after October of the following year, and other factors, and balancing the responsibilities of each party, this court determines Yakun Company's losses as follows: principal loss for weight shortage of RMB 1,060,390 plus interest (calculated at the People's Bank of China contemporaneous demand deposit rate from January 12, 2004, until the date of actual payment), and loss for quality downgrade of RMB 444,480.80. Yakun Company's other claims are dismissed.

In summary, the judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact, and the application of law was correct in all parts except for the erroneous calculation of losses and the omission of the weight shortage loss. Yakun Company's ground of appeal for compensation for weight shortage loss is established, and Kangrui Company's ground of appeal that it should not bear the market risk loss is established. These are supported by this court. The ground of appeal of Yakun Company that Kangrui Company should bear all losses and the ground of appeal of Kangrui Company that it should bear no losses are both not supported by this court. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (1) and (2) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*, this court hereby orders as follows:

1. Affirm Item 3 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2004) Xin Er Chu Zi No. 114 of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, and the allocation of the court acceptance fee and preservation fee for the first instance;
2. Reverse Item 1 of the main text of that civil judgment;
3. Amend Item 2 of the main text of that civil judgment to read: Xinjiang Jinghe County Kangrui Cotton Processing Co., Ltd. shall compensate Xinjiang Yakun Trading Co., Ltd. for cotton principal loss of RMB 444,480.80, principal loss of RMB 1,060,390, and interest (calculated at the People's Bank of China contemporaneous demand deposit rate from January 12, 2004, until the date of actual payment).

The above amounts payable shall be paid within 10 days from the date of service of this judgment. For late payment, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 232 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*.

The court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 129,976.74, of which Xinjiang Yakun Trading Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 103,981.39, and Xinjiang Jinghe County Kangrui Cotton Processing Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 25,995.35.

This judgment is final.
